recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Do not add duplicate prose or another invariant unless Patient Care later changes whether missing role/member should remain only a warning or best-practice condition.
issue_request: FHIR-26421 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care R5 change request asking for an invariant on CareTeam.participant requiring at least one of role or member while both elements remain 0..1; Jira comments specified a warning or best-practice invariant using role.exists() or member.exists().
initial_application: Commit 1b49161451944185626348ae983487055a76652b, titled 'J#20012 CareTeam name search parameter; J#26421 CareTeam invariant', added ctm-2 to source/careteam/structuredefinition-CareTeam.xml as a warning with expression role.exists() or member.exists(). The same commit also included an unrelated J#20012 CareTeam name search-parameter change.
additional_context: CareTeam is active in source/fhir.ini, has ctm as its abbreviation, and is marked approved. Later CareTeam work for FHIR-42928 removed the separate onBehalfOf/member-is-Practitioner invariant and briefly renumbered the role/member invariant before restoring it to ctm-2; it did not supersede or remove the FHIR-26421 rule. Community searches found Patient Care meeting context for FHIR-26421 and no direct Zulip or Confluence evidence contradicting the source/Jira conclusion.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current authoritative CareTeam StructureDefinition contains ctm-2 on CareTeam.participant with severity warning and expression role.exists() or member.exists(), and CareTeam.participant.role and CareTeam.participant.member reference condition ctm-2. The current ctm-2 invariant-test fixture still includes a participant lacking both role and member.
